page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m1.large is a burstable virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned at the lower end of the spectrum. The burstable CPU allocation model restricts sustained high-compute workloads, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1255.78 and a multi-core score of 2507.5, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a read-only large block bandwidth of 20.37 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 880.99, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested configurations.

Given the burstable CPU allocation and low resource density, the ecs.t6-c1m1.large is designed for low-intensity, intermittent workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for entry-level tasks that do not require continuous CPU utilization, such as lightweight microservices, development environments, or basic static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 2.37 GB/sec in testing. It is not suitable for database operations, large-scale data processing, or memory-intensive applications.
